title: The checkout had no set-group-ID while the clone wrote, so nested entries kept gid 0 and the execution could not read them
resolution: The checkout is created with the execution group and mode 2700 before the clone; a privileged Linux test reads and edits nested entries, failing with the old 0700

title: After a restart a new reclaim could run while the previous reclaim program still ran, with nothing to identify or wait for it
resolution: The hand-off record names the reclaim program's containment, which must be proven empty before another reclaim, Git work, or hand-off; item 16 tests a surviving program

title: On macOS the mode never changes, so the hand-off state that Git refusals depend on was lost on restart
resolution: The hand-off state is a worker record in the attempt directory on every platform; a double test that keeps the mode closed after a hand-off failed before and passes

title: Startup changed the group and mode of worker/workspaces without checking it, so a link there opened a control-record directory
resolution: The start checks now cover worker/workspaces against links and foreign owners; a unit test with the root linked to the journal directory failed before and passes

title: The double's reclaim copied hard-linked files through a predictable name, writing through a planted link or over a project file
resolution: The copy is made under a random name with exclusive create from a source opened without following links; a test plants a link, a hard link, and a file under the old name

title: The double's reclaim derived group bits from the owner bits, so files of mode 0000 or 0400 stayed closed and hard-linked ones failed to copy
resolution: Files now get 0660, or 0770 when executable, before any copy; a test with 0000 and 0500 files, one hard-linked, failed before and passes

title: A deleted .git made the double reject its promise instead of returning the unsafe-checkout failure
resolution: A missing .git is refused as unsafe-checkout; the conformance case now deletes .git of a second workspace and checks inspect, snapshot, push, and remove

title: Never setting safe.directory does not keep Git's ownership check when inherited configuration or SUDO_UID trusts other owners
resolution: The adapter checks the owners itself and runs Git without system or global configuration, inherited GIT_CONFIG values, or SUDO_UID; the harness list starts with a reset

title: The contract refused every push of a handed-off workspace with workspace-handed-off, while the double checked the kind and credential first
resolution: The contract and delta now fix the refusal order of all operations as the double has it; the conformance case checks foreign and at-head pushes while handed off

title: The planned Linux test forbade the agent to list any directory under worker/, its own handed-off checkout included
resolution: The test and section 2 now forbid listing the path to the checkout and control-record directories and allow listing the handed-off checkout

title: The records presented review pass 3 as an unconditional gate although governance ends the review after a Low-only pass
resolution: Task 3.2 and the remaining gates now require pass 3 only if pass 2 has findings above Low

title: The slot was free at the execution's exit while the reclaim program still ran as the shared account, so a next execution could signal or trace it
resolution: The worker counts a handed-off workspace as holding its slot until the reclaim and declares capacity again after it; handOff refuses a second one with other-workspace-handed-off; conformance case and defect variant

title: A failed reclaim program had no defined outcome, and without fs.protected_hardlinks an agent could link a control record into its checkout
resolution: A failed program keeps the workspace handed off, reclaim fails with reclaim-failed, reported, not rerun; the worker refuses to start unless fs.protected_hardlinks is 1; item 16 tests

title: A gitfile below the checkout's top, such as a submodule's, let the worker's Git open and refresh another workspace's Git directory
resolution: The check refuses any .git entry below the top as unsafe-checkout and the adapter's Git never recurses into submodules; the double and a conformance case cover a nested gitfile, failing before

title: The scenario Delegated child on a second worker stated a placement outcome that the workspace port cannot test
resolution: Kept where the coordinator placed it, rephrased as the worker's testable refusal of the child while the parent's workspace is handed off, with the placement on another worker as its consequence

title: G3 plan rows 37 and 41 do not carry the item 41 decision, and rows 18 and 21 do not carry the contract's new obligations
resolution: The coordinator forbade editing docs/g3-plan.md and D14 for this decision; only row 16 may change, and it now names the pass 2 obligations of item 16

title: The double created .git before it made the checkout set-group-ID, the reverse of the contract's order
resolution: The double creates the checkout with 2700 before .git; a Linux test that .git inherits the set-group-ID bit failed before and passes

title: The double's reclaim opened every non-directory as a file, so a hard-linked named pipe blocked it forever
resolution: Only regular files are copied, checked before opening; the contract says so; a test with a hard-linked named pipe hung before and passes

title: Giving the group read and write allowed keeping set-user-ID or sticky bits, and a sticky directory blocks the worker's removal
resolution: The reclaim program sets exactly 0660 or 0770 on files and 2770 on directories, clearing other bits, in the contract, the delta, and the design

title: Section 2 said the clone's entries are group-writable, but Git writes object files read-only
resolution: The table now says the group gets the owner's bits under umask 0007, read-only where Git writes read-only

title: The scenario Inherited safe.directory passes through the owner check alone and does not test the configuration scope rule
resolution: Added the scenario Inherited command-scope configuration, a GIT_CONFIG_COUNT core.hooksPath and a global insteadOf, and the item 16 test

title: The list of agent-controlled .git/config settings the adapter ignores was open, missing keys such as http.proxy, include.path, and pushurl
resolution: The adapter writes .git/config anew from the workspace record before each Git call; scenario Agent-written repository settings and an item 16 test

title: The double checked for another hand-off record and wrote its own in separate steps, so two concurrent hand-offs both succeeded
resolution: The double serializes the check and the write per workspace root; the contract and spec require it per worker; a conformance case of two concurrent hand-offs and a defect variant
